properties.name: Alto Maipo (Puente Alto & Pirque)
properties.category: The undisputed Kingdom of South American Cabernet Sauvignon: cassis, wild mint, eucalyptus, cedar, graphite, and silky aristocratic tannins (Almaviva, Don Melchor, Viñedo Chadwick, Seña).
properties.description: Located immediately south of Santiago in the high Andean foothills, Puente Alto and Pirque are the historical ground zero for Chilean fine wine.
properties.source: Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional (BCN) / IDE Chile

properties.name: Colchagua Valley & Apalta Amphitheater
properties.category: Monumental, opulent Carmenère and luxury red blends: dark blackberry, cocoa nibs, black pepper, grilled bell pepper, and velvety chocolate tannins (Clos Apalta, Montes Folly, Neyen).
properties.description: Regarded as the 'Napa Valley of Chile', Apalta earned official D.O. status in 2018 for its world-class luxury red blends.
properties.source: Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional (BCN) / IDE Chile

properties.name: Casablanca & San Antonio / Leyda Valley
properties.category: Laser-focused, aromatic Sauvignon Blanc (grapefruit, lime, jalapeño, sea spray) and elegant, mineral-driven coastal Pinot Noir and Chardonnay.
properties.description: Pioneered in 1982 by Pablo Morandé, Casablanca transformed Chile from a purely red wine country into a world leader in cool-climate whites.
properties.source: Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional (BCN) / IDE Chile

properties.name: Peumo & Cachapoal Valley
properties.category: The undisputed world capital for 100% single-varietal Carmenère: silky blueberry, black plum, tobacco, dark chocolate, and sweet paprika without vegetal bitterness (Carmín de Peumo, Terrunyo).
properties.description: The historical sanctuary where Carmenère was preserved and rediscovered in 1994 by French ampelographer Jean-Michel Boursiquot.
properties.source: Biblioteca del Congreso Nacional (BCN) / IDE Chile
